items.statement: In the intakes from October 2026 to October 2027, a month-3 Transition Check score of 30 or below will have a sensitivity of at least 0.65 and a specificity of at least 0.60 for separation from the hospital within 12 months of hire.
items.rationale: Need and practice change are high because the booster plan depends on the answer; novelty is modest because one external estimate exists; feasibility is high because the score and the dates are already collected.
items.risks: Fewer separations than expected would widen the intervals; a change in seminar timing would change the index test.

items.statement: Adding stated intention to leave at month 6 to the month-3 score will raise sensitivity without lowering specificity below 0.60.
items.rationale: Intention alone misses half of leavers (claim c4), but it might add information to the score.
items.risks: A second question adds resident time and an extra test to pre-specify.

items.statement: The cut-off is less accurate for residents on night-heavy rotations than for those on day-heavy rotations.
items.rationale: Night work may change both transition scores and reasons for leaving.
items.risks: Too few separations in each group for more than a descriptive comparison.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the single accuracy target that decides the booster plan.
